tasks.title: Separate CI N/A from retained changed-line evidence
tasks.objective: Remove the incentive to add unrelated executable code when a product change has no changed executable denominator, while preserving explicit retained-evidence and owner-floor guarantees.
tasks.outcome: CI reports zero-denominator product changes honestly as N/A instead of manufacturing a coverage proof or forcing an unrelated executable edit, while retained changed-line evidence remains non-empty and fail-closed.
acceptance: Changed-line auto mode reports N/A when the current product change has no executable added or modified line; N/A is visibly distinct from a passing changed-line percentage and is never recorded as changed-line coverage evidence.

Filesystem source inventory, all seven owner groups, fixed 90/85/95 floors, missing-report checks, and the ordinary repository Gate still execute for documentation, comment-only, deletion-only, rename, and untracked product changes.

Explicit true retained-evidence mode still requires an explicit valid base, direct or merge-base semantics, a nonzero executable denominator, and at least 90 percent coverage; it never degrades to N/A.

When auto mode has a nonzero executable denominator it still enforces the 90 percent floor, including mixed executable and non-executable changes without counting deleted or comment-only lines as executable evidence.

Policy tests cover documentation-only, comment-only, deletion-only, rename, untracked, mixed executable/non-executable, passing and failing executable percentages, and explicit retained-evidence behavior.

Testing strategy, contributor guidance, CI evidence-map language, and Tracker verification distinguish owner qualification, auto N/A, and retained changed-line proof without weakening T-020's seven-owner result.

verification.proves: All owner floors pass and the corrected auto versus explicit changed-line semantics execute on instrumented reports.
CI N/A and retained-evidence meanings are public, distinct, and do not invite a fake executable denominator.

tasks.title: Bind required CI Gates to one neutralized execution boundary
tasks.objective: Prevent an earlier workflow step from using persisted shell startup state to mutate the checkout or weaken required Gate environment after source identity was verified.
tasks.outcome: Each required critical and coverage Gate starts with inert shell startup files, verifies the exact clean checkout, and immediately executes the canonical Gate inside one final step that has no post-fence runner boundary.
acceptance: The independent source-fence step is removed. Critical and coverage each have exactly one unconditional final Gate step whose exact inline command neutralizes inherited shell and Git redirection state, verifies the checked-out HEAD and complete worktree against the event source identity, and immediately execs the canonical Gate with no intervening runner step or repository helper.

The final step explicitly binds BASH_ENV and ENV to /dev/null before Bash startup, unsets those variables before the nested Gate Bash, invokes a platform-owned Bash without profile or rc files, and retains the exact required CTXMUX, tmux, fuzz, model, and coverage environment. Ubuntu 24.04 and macOS 15 remain the only claimed lanes.

The identity check cannot be redirected by PATH or the common GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_COMMON_DIR, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, or GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES environment channels; it uses the platform Git binary and the workflow event SHA rather than a mutable prior-step value.

Deterministic validator and shell-process oracles reproduce first-shell-noop/second-shell BASH_ENV mutation, show that same-step composition without startup neutralization is still unsafe, and reject missing or changed startup bindings, split fence/Gate steps, weakened identity checks, altered Gate invocations, and helper-only self-verification for both required jobs.

Canonical checkout, job matrix, triggers, required platforms, no-skip/no-retry rules, exact source inventory, seven coverage owners, 90/85/95 floors, changed-line base semantics, and full test selection remain unchanged and continue to pass the ordinary repository Gate.

The correction stays inside GitHub required-step and CI-reachability ownership. It adds no reusable workflow-security framework and makes no claim against hostile runners, arbitrary actions or background processes, dynamic-loader injection, complete toolchain or PATH attestation, Git object-store tampering, Windows, or self-hosted runners.

T-020 and T-023 remain immutable historical evidence; this task records the later CI execution-boundary correction, independent adversarial review, exact commit/message audit, and formal Gate under its own receipt.

verification.proves: The startup-hook negative oracles, canonical required workflow, CI reachability, ordinary tests, and public Gates pass together.
Critical and coverage use the same reviewed startup-neutralized final-step execution contract.

tasks.title: Fence daemon shutdown socket cleanup by bound identity
tasks.objective: Make socket cleanup symmetric across startup and shutdown so an exiting daemon cannot unlink a different listener that replaced its published pathname.
tasks.outcome: The daemon removes only the Unix socket identity it successfully bound, while independently substituted live listeners remain reachable after the old daemon exits.
acceptance: The shutdown guard retains the bound socket device and inode after successful bind and unlinks the pathname only while it still names that identity.
A real replacement listener can take over the pathname before the old daemon exits; old-daemon shutdown preserves the replacement path and new connections still reach it.

Missing, non-socket, symlink, or different-socket replacements are never removed, and documentation keeps pathname recheck versus unlink non-atomicity in a hostile writable parent as a residual boundary.

verification.proves: The real replacement-listener shutdown regression and the complete native lifecycle gate pass.

tasks.title: Correlate attachment controls and expose applied terminal size
tasks.objective: Give low-latency persistent attachments deterministic per-command outcomes and real PTY size observability without inventing a general transaction system.
tasks.outcome: Consumers can pipeline input, resize, and stop, match every acceptance or error to its command, repair size drift, and distinguish accepted stop from final exit.
acceptance: Every attachment input, resize, and stop command carries a bounded opaque command id, and every accepted or error result echoes it without confusing command results with output or lifecycle events.

The contract states the exact owner boundary reached by acceptance: input is accepted only after the daemon's PTY write boundary succeeds, resize reports the size read back from the owning PTY, and stop acceptance remains separate from terminal Exited.

Command ids provide correlation, not permission to replay uncertain input; duplicate, reconnect, and unknown-disposition behavior is explicit and fails closed unless a separately proven deduplication contract applies.

A real PTY fixture pipelines at least 1000 ordered input chunks plus concurrent resize and stop, proves exact result matching, bytes and applied size, and covers rejection, disconnect, late result, backpressure, and final-output ordering.
Short-lived request methods and persistent Attachment methods present compatible semantics through the public SDK without a second command bus or Agent-specific acknowledgement layer.

The current daemon incarnation has one explicit PTY control-owner boundary for input, resize, stop, and future quiesce; durable Run facts are not mislabeled as live authority, and the change adds no public actor, Backend hierarchy, or duplicate runtime graph solely for implementation shape.

Bounded input backpressure cannot starve resize or stop, and the real PTY fixture preserves fragmented opaque terminal input including SGR mouse and bracketed-paste sequences without interpreting them as UI or Agent semantics.

verification.proves: Protocol, SDK, real PTY, pipelined control, control-under-input-saturation, opaque mouse/paste bytes, applied-size, disconnect, and lifecycle ordering regressions pass.
Attachment command resolution, correlation, retry limits, applied size, and stop-versus-exit semantics are documented for clean consumers.

tasks.title: Close unpublished-child rollback before creation-key reuse
tasks.objective: Make the shared Start/Fork publication boundary retain direct-child and exact-key ownership across a pre-COMMIT persistence rejection until the child-handle owner proves terminal-and-reaped, so a same-key retry cannot create a second process.
tasks.outcome: Every rejected persistent creation either proves its ctxmux-owned direct child reaped before the key becomes reusable or transfers child ownership and an exact-key fence into bounded private cleanup accounting without indefinitely consuming an unrelated key stripe or global launch permit.
acceptance: Deterministic owner-controlled Start and Fork fixtures launch a real direct child, force persistence rejection before COMMIT, and prove kill plus reap, no published Run/key mapping, and an unrelated-process sentinel untouched.

Terminal-and-reaped proof comes from the waiter that owns the child handle; public RunState, a cached PID, elapsed time, or a log line is never treated as cleanup proof, and stop, kill, wait, or waiter-channel failure cannot be ignored.

Until reap is proven, the existing creation owner retains the child and exact key or safely transfers both to one globally bounded daemon-private cleanup owner; a transfer may release the shared stripe and global launch permit only after the exact-key fence is independently installed.

An unresolved cleanup is reported explicitly, remains visible to bounded accounting and daemon shutdown, and cannot be multiplied without bound by changing operation keys; it publishes no fake Run and creates no PID-based signalling fallback.

Concurrent same-key retry during cleanup converges on the existing owner or an explicit fenced failure without a second launch; after proven cleanup exactly one new leader may reuse the key, while unrelated keys retain launch progress.
Normal persistence capacity rejection remains recoverable and does not poison unrelated append or finalize operations; fatal storage failure classification remains unchanged.
The correction requalifies T-012 public Start/Fork duplicate concurrency, response loss, conflicting reuse, post-COMMIT publication, restart recovery, Rust client, CLI, and TypeScript SDK behavior.

Protocol and architecture truth distinguish proven rollback key reuse from an unresolved exact-key fence, while daemon crash still promises no persistent pending tombstone, process adoption, or descendant cleanup.

The correction stays inside creation, native child ownership, and persistence admission; it adds no Session identity, process-tree policy, persistent pending tombstone, public transaction API, Backend framework, or general fault-injection system.

verification.proves: Real-child persistence rejection, kill/reap, same-key concurrency, unrelated identity, persistence actor, and full repository regressions pass.
